t: GMAT: NASA's Open-Source Mission Design Tool
title: GMAT: NASA's Open-Source Mission Design Tool
description: The General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT) is NASA Goddard's open-source space trajectory optimization and mission analysis system, developed with private-sector contributors. It designs trajectories from low Earth orbit to interplanetary cruise, and it has supported real missions including LRO, LADEE, OSIRIS-REx, and TESS. It is free, scriptable, and runs on desktop workstations.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Propagators: Moving the Spacecraft
description: A propagator numerically integrates the spacecraft's equations of motion: GMAT offers Runge-Kutta 89, Prince-Dormand 78, and other integrators with adaptive step control. The integrator picks small steps where dynamics are fast (perigee) and large steps where they are slow (apogee). Accuracy settings trade compute time against trajectory error.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

t: Force Models: What Pushes the Spacecraft
title: Force Models: What Pushes the Spacecraft
description: GMAT's force models decide which physics the propagator integrates: point-mass gravity plus high-order gravity fields, atmospheric drag, solar radiation pressure, and third-body gravity from the Sun and Moon. Drag needs an atmosphere model and a spacecraft area-to-mass; SRP needs reflectivity. Leaving out a real force is how trajectories quietly go wrong.

title: Finite Burns: Modeling Real Maneuvers
description: Real maneuvers are finite burns — the engine fires for minutes, and the thrust direction and mass flow shape the trajectory during the burn. GMAT models impulsive burns for quick studies and finite burns with thruster data for flight fidelity. Burn execution errors (magnitude, pointing) become dispersions in Monte Carlo analysis.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Targeting: Hitting the Aim Point
description: Targeting solves for the maneuver that hits the aim point: GMAT's differential corrector varies control variables (burn components, epochs) until constraints (altitude, B-plane, arrival conditions) are met. It is Newton-style iteration on a trajectory — propagate, measure the miss, correct, repeat. Most mission design is targeting loops.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Estimators: Orbit Determination
description: GMAT's estimators turn tracking measurements into orbit knowledge: batch least-squares fits long arcs of data, and the extended Kalman filter processes measurements sequentially. Estimation needs a measurement model (range, Doppler) plus station locations and media corrections. The covariance out of the estimator sizes every maneuver and every pointing budget.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: GMAT Scripting: The Mission Script
description: A GMAT mission is a script: create spacecraft and propagators, set initial conditions, then a mission sequence of Propagate, Maneuver, and Achieve commands. Scripts are text, version-controlled, and reviewable — the mission design is literally readable. GUIs generate the same scripts underneath.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Coordinate Systems and Time
description: Trajectory work lives or dies on frames and time: GMAT handles Earth-centered inertial, Moon-centered, and rotating frames, plus UTC, TAI, and ephemeris time conversions. A maneuver computed in the wrong frame misses by thousands of kilometers. Frame discipline is a core mission-design skill the tool enforces.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Optimization: Finding the Best Trajectory
description: GMAT's optimizers search maneuver variables for minimum fuel or minimum time subject to constraints — the same targeting machinery with an objective function. Low-thrust spirals and multi-burn sequences are optimizer territory. The optimizer needs good initial guesses, which is why designers still sketch trajectories by hand first.

title: LRO: GMAT at the Moon
description: The Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter mission used GMAT-class trajectory design for its lunar orbit insertion and station-keeping in the Moon's lumpy gravity field. Low lunar orbits are unstable — mascons tug constantly — so the design included regular maintenance maneuvers. GMAT's force models and targeting handled it.

title: OSIRIS-REx: Touching an Asteroid
description: OSIRIS-REx's journey to the asteroid Bennu and its touch-and-go sample collection were designed with GMAT-class tools: interplanetary cruise targeting, proximity operations around a tiny spinning body, and the precise TAG maneuver. Milligravity proximity ops are the extreme edge of trajectory design.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: TESS: The Lunar Flyby Trick
description: TESS rides a clever 2:1 lunar-resonant high Earth orbit designed with GMAT-class analysis: a lunar flyby pumps the orbit into a stable resonance that needs almost no maintenance. The trajectory does the work that propellant would otherwise do. Mission design at its most elegant.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Validation: Trusting the Numbers
description: GMAT is validated against known solutions: two-body spot checks, published trajectories, and cross-comparison with independent tools. Validation is never 'it ran' — it is quantified error against truth. Every mission re-validates the configurations it actually flies.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Ephemeris: Where Everything Is
description: GMAT pulls planet and Moon positions from ephemeris files (DE series) so every propagation uses the same solar system everyone else uses. Third-body forces and eclipse calculations depend on it. Consistent ephemerides are why two teams get the same trajectory.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

t: The Full GMAT Mission Design Loop
title: The Full GMAT Mission Design Loop
description: The ladder-top GMAT loop: sketch the trajectory, script the mission, propagate with full force models, target the aim points, optimize the fuel, estimate with tracking data, validate against truth, and fly. Fifteen rungs up, that loop designed real missions to the Moon, asteroids, and deep space — open source, on a workstation.
